faq.q: Is July too hot for a yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Not at all. July averages 30°C, but the sea breeze and yacht's bimini keep it comfortable. Most boats have shaded decks and cabins with A/C. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and light clothing. The water is 23°C – perfect for swimming.

faq.q: What is the best time of day to charter in July?
faq.a: Morning charters from 10:00 to 16:00 avoid the strongest heat and afternoon wind. Sunset cruises (18:00–21:00) are also popular – temperatures drop to 22°C and the light over La Concha is stunning.

faq.q: Does it ever rain in Marbella in July?
faq.a: Virtually none. July averages 0 mm of rainfall. You can expect clear blue skies every day. The only weather variable is wind – usually light easterly Levante at 10–15 knots, which is fine for all our boats.

faq.q: Which boats are best for hot July days?
faq.a: Flybridge models like Azimut 58 Flybridge or Mangusta 80 offer shaded upper decks and good airflow. For smaller groups, the Azimut 39 or Astondoa 40 have spacious cockpits with awnings. All include soft drinks, water, beer, and cava.

faq.q: What should I bring on a July yacht charter?
faq.a: Sunscreen (SPF 50+), sunglasses, a hat, swimwear, a light cover-up, and a towel. The boat provides drinks and snacks. A windbreaker is optional for the afternoon breeze. Don't forget your camera – the coast looks incredible.

faq.q: How rough is the sea in Marbella in July?
faq.a: Generally calm. The Mediterranean is sheltered by the Costa del Sol coast. Morning seas are glassy; afternoons see a light chop from the Levante wind. Our 12m+ yachts handle it easily. If you're prone to seasickness, book a morning charter or a larger catamaran like Lagoon 380.

faq.q: Can I swim in the sea in July?
faq.a: Yes – sea temperature averages 23°C, which is warm and refreshing. Popular swimming spots include Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, and the coves near Cabopino. All charters include stops for swimming.

faq.q: What is the sunset time in Marbella in July?

data.body_html:
July in Marbella delivers textbook Mediterranean summer weather: blazing sunshine, warm seas, and barely a cloud in the sky. With average highs of 30°C, sea temperatures of 23°C, and 11 hours of daily sun, it's the peak season for Marbella yacht charter – and for good reason. This guide covers everything you need to know about July conditions, which boats suit the heat best, and how to dodge the afternoon breeze.

July Weather Overview: What to Expect

July is the hottest and driest month in Marbella. Expect zero rainfall, UV index 9+, and a steady easterly Levante wind at 10–15 knots. The breeze kicks up around 14:00, creating a light chop offshore – but nothing that bothers a 12m+ yacht. Morning sea glass is common, making early charters ideal for smooth cruising.

  • Average high: 30°C (86°F)
  • Average low: 22°C (72°F)
  • Sea temperature: 23°C (73°F)
  • Sunshine: 11 hours/day
  • Wind: Levante (E), 10–15 knots
  • Rainfall: 0 mm

Best Times to Charter in July

The sweet spot is 10:00 to 16:00 – you get calm seas, high sun, and the best swimming light at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Alternatively, sunset charters from 18:00 to 21:00 offer cooler temps (22°C) and spectacular views of La Concha. Evening charters are particularly popular on the Azimut 58 Flybridge and Mangusta 80, where the flybridge becomes the best seat in the house.

Which Boats Handle July Heat Best?

For maximum comfort, choose a boat with shade and airflow. Our flybridge models – Azimut 58 Flybridge, Mangusta 80, and Maiora 26m – offer shaded upper decks with panoramic views. The Azimut 39 and Astondoa 40 have deep cockpits with awnings. All charters include unlimited soft drinks, water, beer, and cava. If you want a jet ski to cool off, the Mangusta 80 (white or grey) includes one free on 4-hour bookings (€4,719 min).

Wind & Sea Conditions: What to Know

The Levante wind is the dominant pattern in July. It blows from the east, often picking up after lunch. This creates a short chop of 0.3–0.6m in the open sea, but the coast near Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina remains sheltered. Our 12m+ yachts handle it with ease. If you're sensitive to motion, book a morning charter or choose the catamaran Lagoon 380 – its twin hulls reduce roll significantly.

What to Wear & Pack for July Chartering

Lightweight, breathable fabrics are key. Swimwear, a cover-up, and non-slip deck shoes are standard. Bring a hat and SPF 50+ sunscreen – the UV is intense. A light windbreaker is useful for the afternoon breeze. The boat provides towels, but you may want your own for swimming. Evening charters call for a light jacket or sweater – the drop to 22°C feels cool after the heat.

Swimming & Snorkelling Spots in July

July's 23°C sea is perfect for swimming. Top spots include Cala del Faro (east of Marbella), Cala Cortés (near Cabopino), and the coves off the Golden Mile. Water visibility is excellent – often 15–20m – making snorkelling rewarding. All charters include stops at your choice of location.

How to Book Your July Charter

July is peak season – boats book weeks ahead. The Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day (8 hours), including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. The Mangusta 80 requires a minimum 4-hour booking at €4,719 and includes a jet ski. For other boats, pricing is on request via WhatsApp. Check availability for your dates and secure your spot early.
